stemMd: A 0.25 mol sample of CaCl₂ dissolves completely. Assuming complete dissociation, how many moles of chloride ions are produced?
explanationMd: The dissolution equation is CaCl₂ → Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻. Each mole of calcium chloride gives two moles of chloride ions, so 0.25 mol gives 0.50 mol. Total ion amount would be different because it also includes calcium.

distractorRationale.a: Each formula unit supplies two chloride ions, not one.
distractorRationale.d: This divides by two instead of multiplying.
distractorRationale.c: This counts all ions, including calcium, rather than chloride alone.
distractorRationale.b: This assigns four chloride ions per formula unit.
